Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). This page is the single source of truth for what live-ops events are scheduled, on which game, and at what cadence. It pairs with the runtime that actually fires these events — for architecture, the scheduler's known fragility, and the July 2025 outage, see Live-Ops Event Engine. Event goals are set against the metrics bar tracked in Product OKRs — 2025 H1.

Event calendar

Every timed event we have run or currently run across the portfolio. \"Cadence\" is how the slot recurs; \"status\" is where the event stands as of the latest planning review.

EventGameCadenceStatus
Nathan's Treasure HuntDomino Delights (\"Game of Dominoes\" / GoD)One-off seasonalShipped Apr 2025
Win & CollectDomino DelightsOne-off seasonalShipped Sep 2024
River RushDomino DelightsOne-off seasonalShipped Jan 2025
Plague RaceZombie Match 3D (\"Puzzles vs Zombies\")RecurringLive; algo bug Aug 2025
Zombie LaneZombie Match 3DOne-off seasonalShipped Jul 2025
Endless Monster ModeZombie Match 3DRecurring monthly (from Jun 2025)Live

Notes on individual events

  • Nathan's Treasure Hunt — our best-performing GoD seasonal to date; the reward-ladder structure is the template we now reuse for one-off events.
  • Plague Race — the recurring ranked competition on ZM3D. A scoring/matchmaking algorithm bug surfaced in Aug 2025 and skewed leaderboard settlement; treat pre-fix cohorts with caution when reading event revenue.
  • Endless Monster Mode — a monthly recurring mode that has become the reliable mid-month engagement beat since Jun 2025. This is the anchor slot the calendar is built around.

July 2025 scheduler outage. The event/lives scheduler stalled for roughly two weeks in July 2025, so scheduled events did not fire and the published calendar diverged from what players actually saw. Do not backfill or reason about that window from this calendar — the Live-Ops Event Engine page holds the reconstructed timeline and the revenue impact.

Planning cadence

We are a ~16-person studio, so live-ops planning is deliberately lightweight — one recurring meeting and one shared calendar, not a dedicated ops team. The working rhythm:

  • Weekly slotting review (Mondays). Design (Julia) and Growth (Frederick) walk the next four weeks: which recurring slots fire (Endless Monster Mode monthly, Plague Race on its ranked cadence) and whether a one-off seasonal drops on top.
  • Two-week content lock. Event config — reward tables, windows, cohort targeting — must be authored and reviewed at least two weeks before the window opens, so QA has a full sprint to validate on staging.
  • No overlapping recurring competitions. We do not run two ranked events on the same game at once; it splits the leaderboard population and muddies the revenue read.
  • Post-event read. Each event gets a short retro against its target from Product OKRs before the slot is reused.

The recurring slots (Endless Monster Mode monthly; Plague Race ranked) are the backbone of the calendar. One-off seasonals like Nathan's Treasure Hunt are layered on for spikes — they are the exception, not the base cadence, and should never displace a recurring slot without sign-off from Frederick.

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). This page is the map of our Metabase dashboards. Analysts run everything against the Snowflake BI layer, which is fed from the S3 event lake \u2014 for how telemetry gets from the Unity client into that warehouse, see Analytics Integration \u2014 Unity \u2192 Snowflake.

Metabase is the reporting front-end only \u2014 it holds saved questions and dashboards, not the source of truth. Every card queries Snowflake marts. If a dashboard looks stale, check the warehouse load first (the COPY runs on a schedule), not Metabase.

Standard dashboards

These are the dashboards we keep pinned and review on a regular cadence. They cover the full loop from acquisition through retention and monetization. Names are illustrative \u2014 the actual collection names in Metabase may differ slightly, but the purpose and audience below are what matters.

DashboardPurposeAudience
DAU & RetentionDaily active users, session length, and D1/D7/D30 retention curves by title and cohort.Whole studio; reviewed at Monday standup.
FTUE FunnelFirst-time-user-experience completion \u2014 level start / complete / fail drop-off through the onboarding funnel.Product & game design.
UA / CPI / ROAS by ChannelUser acquisition performance \u2014 spend, installs, blended and per-channel CPI, and D7/D30 ROAS, joined from Singular attribution.Growth/UA (Frederick); exec on investor prep.
Monetization \u2014 IAP / ARPUIn-app-purchase revenue, ARPU / ARPPU, conversion, and Season Pass attach + completion.Product & finance.
Live-Event PerformanceParticipation, completion, and revenue lift per live event vs baseline days.Live-ops & product.

How to read them

  • Every card is date-partitioned; default range is the trailing 28 days. Widen the filter for launch-window cohort views.
  • UA numbers reconcile to Singular, not to store console \u2014 attribution windows differ, so expect small deltas.
  • Retention is measured on activity, not installs; a reinstall inside the window counts as a returning user, not a new one.

Metric definitions live with the OKRs

This page tells you which dashboard to open. It does not define what a metric means. D1 retention, blended CPI, D30 ROAS, ARPU \u2014 those definitions, and the targets we hold them to, are owned alongside the objectives in Product OKRs \u2014 2025 H1. If a dashboard number and an OKR number disagree, the OKR definition wins and the Metabase card is the thing to fix.

Do not fork a dashboard to \"redefine\" a metric for one analysis. If you need a variant (e.g. per-channel D1 instead of blended), add a card to the existing collection so the definition stays traceable. Silent metric drift between a fork and the canonical card is how two people end up quoting different D1 numbers in the same meeting.

Titles currently instrumented into these dashboards: Zombie Match 3D (store name Puzzles vs Zombies), Domino Delights (codename GoD), and Combo Fighter. All three share one event pipeline, so the same dashboard filters to any title.

Welcome to Harmony Games, Inc. (harmonygames.co). This is the studio overview for new hires — who we are, what we're building, and how we work. Read it first, then jump to the space for your discipline.

Who we are

Harmony Games is a small, remote-first mobile-game studio, founded in March 2023 and incorporated the following month in Delaware. We build hybrid-casual puzzle games — titles with the instant approachability of a casual game and the retention hooks of a light RPG. The team is distributed across three continents and runs lean by design (around sixteen people at its peak), keeping everyone close to the product.

The founding thesis comes from a specific background: 10+ years in gaming marketing plus a psychology degree. That pairing is the whole company in one sentence — we sit on the seam between marketing and product, and build games where the acquisition funnel and the core loop are designed together rather than handed off.

Mission

“A game of dominoes is really just match-3 in disguise — the same metrics, the same funnel. The opportunity is to take that casual approachability and deepen it: collection mechanics and a light RPG economy that give a player a reason to come back on day 30. Bridge marketing and product, and you get a game that is both cheap to acquire for and worth staying in.”

What we're building

Our titles, in the order the studio's focus moved to each:

WhenTitleDetail
Mar–Apr 2023Founded & incorporatedHarmony Games, Inc. founded March 2023; Delaware incorporation April 2023.
2023–2024Domino DelightsFirst title (internal codename "Game of Dominoes" / GoD) — tile-match with collection meta; benchmarked against Domino Dreams.
Jan 2025Zombie Match 3DStudio focus shifts to the match-3D RPG (store name "Puzzles vs Zombies"), benchmarked against Match Factory.
2025Combo Fighter (prototype)A third concept taken to prototype to test whether the hybrid-casual formula generalises beyond tile-match.

How we measure success

We measure product ambition against a fundability bar — the retention, CPI, and ROAS a growth round is underwritten on. That scorecard lives in Product OKRs \u2014 2025 H1. Attribution across every title is standardised on Singular.

Where we are today: we've hit our tactical targets (ship dates, CPI), but day-30 retention and payback haven't yet cleared the bar a growth round is priced on. After the October 2025 cost reductions we're running on a lean core team while we pursue a bridge or strategic outcome to fund the next iteration. The near-term focus is proving day-30 retention holds — in hybrid-casual, the marketing-and-product seam only pays off if players stay past day one.

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). Scope: H1 2025 product objectives for Zombie Match 3D (store name Puzzles vs Zombies), scored against the metrics bar our investors expect to see before writing a Series A. This is the working scorecard we reviewed at the mid-year checkpoint.

Framing note: these OKRs were deliberately set to the VC bar for a hybrid-casual title \u2014 the numbers a growth investor needs to see (D1 north of 30%, CPI under $5, early ROAS trending toward payback). Hitting internal comfort levels is not the same as clearing a fundable bar. These are the retention and payback bars the team tracks against each half.

Objectives & Key Results

Global launch on May 15, 2025. Everything below is measured on the four weeks after launch unless noted.

Objective / Key ResultTargetActualStatus
Launch ZM3D globallyMay 15, 2025Shipped May 15, 2025✓ Met
D1 retention> 30%28.4% avg (best week ~30.8%)✗ Missed
Blended CPI< $5.00$4.80✓ Met
D30 ROAS> 0.50.31✗ Missed

Acquisition-channel split

The blended D1 of 28.4% hides a real channel gap. Where the users come from matters as much as how many:

  • Facebook \u2014 D1 landing ~34–39%. Higher intent, better early stickiness, but volume is capped at our budget and CPI creeps up as we scale spend.
  • Unity \u2014 D1 landing ~22–26%. Cheaper, far more volume, but the cohorts churn hard by day two. This channel is what drags the blend under the 30% line.

Practically: we can buy the 30% number on Facebook alone, but not at the volume the model needs, and not without pushing CPI past the $4.80 we booked. Unity gives us scale but poisons retention and ROAS.

Retro & conclusion

Candid retro: we cleared the two levers we control tactically (ship date and CPI) and missed the two that decide fundability (retention and ROAS). A 28.4% D1 with a D30 ROAS of 0.31 is a title that does not pay itself back in the window an investor underwrites. The best single week touched 30%, which tells us the ceiling is close — but a one-week peak is not a durable cohort, and we could not hold it once Unity volume was in the blend.

Net: the ZM3D H1 metrics did not clear the bar a growth round is priced on. That result is what drove the decision to pursue a bridge round rather than a priced Series A — buy time to fix Unity-cohort retention and pull D30 ROAS toward 0.5, then re-approach on stronger numbers. Design context and the intended retention loops live in Zombie Match 3D \u2014 Game Design Document.

H2 follow-ups

  • Rework the FTUE for Unity-sourced installs; the day-two cliff is where the blend breaks.
  • Instrument per-channel D7/D30 ROAS separately (in Singular) so we stop hiding a bad cohort inside a passable blend.
  • Re-baseline the D1 > 30% OKR as a per-channel target, not a blended one.
", "body_format": "storage", "status": "current", "version": 8, "author_id": "user_EMPLOYEE_0008", "created_at": "2025-01-05T12:04:25Z", "updated_at": "2025-08-01T18:20:58Z"}, {"id": "page_zm3d_gdd", "space_id": "space_PROD", "parent_id": "page_prod_home", "title": "Zombie Match 3D \u2014 Game Design Document", "body": "

This is the living Game Design Document for Zombie Match 3D (store title Puzzles vs Zombies). It is the source of truth for the core loop, the RPG combat layer, and monetization. For the coin/life economy see Economy Design \u2014 Coins, Lives & Boosters, and for the paid track see ZM3D Season Pass \u2014 Spec. This document ladders up to Product OKRs \u2014 2025 H1.

Global launch shipped May 15, 2025. This GDD reflects the launch build plus the Season Pass update.

Core mechanic

The matcher is a Match-3D collector benchmarked on Match Factory. Objects sit in a physics pile; the player drags items into a 7-slot tray. Collect any 3 matching objects and they clear from the tray. If all 7 slots fill without a match, the board is lost. Tray pressure is the primary difficulty dial.

  • Pile physics \u2014 objects settle and occlude each other; digging exposes buried matches.
  • 7-slot tray \u2014 the fail state; tuning slot count changes felt difficulty more than object count.
  • Object families \u2014 cosmetic skins that map to elemental ammo in the RPG layer.

Zombie RPG layer

Levels wrap the matcher in combat. Each cleared triple fires the matching element at the current monster. Monsters carry an elemental weakness; hitting the weakness deals bonus damage and can apply a status.

Monster / element table

Monster archetypeWeaknessOn-hit effect
Sparkbound WalkershockChain damage to adjacent enemies
Bloated CarrierpoisonDamage-over-time stack
Charred HuskburnArmor melt
Frostbitten CrawlerfreezeSkips next attack
Bog LurkersplashArea splash to the pack
RioterstunInterrupt current wind-up
Slick RunnerglueMovement pinned
ScreecherblindAttack accuracy drop

Modes

  • Campaign \u2014 authored levels, escalating monster mixes.
  • Endless \u2014 survival board with an item refill every 30s to keep the pile stocked.
  • Infinite-HP Boss \u2014 a damage-race against a boss whose HP does not deplete to zero; the score is total damage dealt before the tray fills.

Monetization

The headline product is the Season Pass at $6.99, launched Jul 15, 2025. It runs a free and a premium reward track over a fixed season window; progression is earned through campaign and Endless play. Coin, life, and booster sinks live in the linked Economy doc \u2014 do not duplicate values here.

Known launch issues (tracked, historical):

  • Hard crash tied to a potion / addressables load path (May 2025) on some devices during first combat.
  • Font-download freeze that stalls the splash screen at ~22% on slow connections.

Boss mode reward config

Owner: Robert (Product). Design: Julia Lawson. Changes to tray count or refill cadence must be reviewed against the OKR dashboard before shipping.

", "body_format": "storage", "status": "current", "version": 11, "author_id": "user_EMPLOYEE_0016", "created_at": "2025-01-20T09:00:52Z", "updated_at": "2025-07-15T11:58:41Z"}, {"id": "page_season_pass_spec", "space_id": "space_PROD", "parent_id": "page_zm3d_gdd", "title": "ZM3D Season Pass \u2014 Spec", "body": "

This is the product spec for the Zombie Match 3D Season Pass (store title Puzzles vs Zombies), written just before launch. The pass is the first recurring paid product on the title and the primary lever we have for lifting ARPU on our existing daily actives. For the core loop, combat layer, and monetization overview this ladders under, see Zombie Match 3D \u2014 Game Design Document, and for the target it serves see Product OKRs \u2014 2025 H1.

At a glance. Launches Jul 15, 2025 at $6.99/month. A free track and a premium track run in parallel over a monthly season window, with rewards unlocked by the same live-ops progression players already earn through play.

Goal & positioning

We monetize almost entirely through consumables (coins, boosters, extra lives). That caps ARPU because it only reaches players already willing to spend on a fail state. The Season Pass adds a low-friction, predictable monthly product that converts engagement \u2014 not frustration \u2014 into revenue, and gives non-payers a visible reason to log in daily via the free track.

  • Cadence \u2014 one season per calendar month; the track resets and re-themes on the 1st.
  • Earn, don't grind \u2014 pass points come from campaign clears, Endless runs, and daily quests. No separate currency to buy.
  • Free track always on \u2014 every player earns from tier 1; the premium track retro-unlocks all already-earned premium rewards at purchase.
  • One SKU \u2014 a single monthly unlock at $6.99. No tier-skips or per-level buys at launch; revisit after we read week-one conversion.

Reward tracks

Each season runs 30 tiers. The free track is deliberately front-loaded so the value of the premium track is legible before a player commits. Premium leans into cosmetics and the coin/gem sinks documented in the economy layer \u2014 it does not sell raw power.

Tier bandFree trackPremium track ($6.99)
1\u20135Coins, 1 boosterSeason avatar frame + coins
6\u201310Extra livesExclusive monster skin
11\u201320CoinsBooster bundles + gems
21\u2013291 boosterCoins, gems, tray cosmetic
30Coin lump sumSignature seasonal skin + gem grant

Points model

Rollout

Ship to 100% on launch day rather than a slow ramp \u2014 the pass is time-boxed to the month, so a partial rollout would leave early cohorts on a shortened first season. We gate on store approval and a live-ops config freeze the day before.

Rollout guardrails:

  • Do not touch tray count or Endless refill cadence during an active season \u2014 it swings the difficulty curve and skews pass-progression pacing right when we're reading purchase intent.
  • Season config (tiers, rewards, theme) is authored in the live-ops tool and locked 24h before the 1st; no hotfixes to reward tables mid-season without Product sign-off.
  • Purchase, tier-claim, and daily-active events are tagged for reporting through our attribution and analytics stack so we can read conversion and IAP mix from day one.

By late summer the Season Pass had grown into a meaningful share of monthly IAP on Zombie Match 3D \u2014 enough that season pacing now factors into every difficulty and live-ops decision on the title. Owner: Robert (Product). Design partner: Julia Lawson.

It is possible that subsequent matches can lead to additional free tile revealed. If a free tile revealed already matches another revealed tile, it is automatically matched. When an auto match happens, the main narration text should say "Auto Matched!"

It is absolutely possible that this can lead into an auto chain of matches that finishes the game automatically, especially when the player is down to < 8 tiles total on the board.

We want this to happen every now and then as it is *very* rewarding to the player's happiness.

When it comes to text effects, this is what we want to do.

**There are 2 types of text:**

1) The main game text that says things like "Excellent", "Great Match" like in Candy Crush. We call this main narration text.

2) Specific individual tile text. This works like the +10 coin pop up text that you see in our mini games and main games when tiles are matched off the board.

**How do we utilize these text in the situation we described above with the combos + text effect? Here is how.**

Whenever a Streak Bonus reveal is fired off and an individual tile is flipped, it will have a small text pop up saying "Streak Bonus Reveal" (Smaller font than narration text)

If this Streak Bonus Reveal ends up as a free match because it happens to match another one on the board, then the main narration will say "Auto Match!"

**Effect Speed:**

We do want chain combos to happen with multiple auto matches happening consecutively, however we do want the full animation of the reveal → the individual text effect "Streak Bonus Reveal" → auto match piece removal from the board → main narration "Auto Matched!" to be *fully played out* and have the same slight pause instead of everything just happening instantly.", "priority": 2, "estimate": null, "due_date": null, "started_at": null, "completed_at": "2024-01-03T06:15:51Z", "canceled_at": null, "archived_at": null, "time_in_status_minutes": 1112478, "labels": ["Improvement", "Mini Game"], "links": [], "relations": [], "is_archived": false, "created_at": "2023-11-03T23:33:54Z", "updated_at": "2024-01-03T06:15:52Z"}], "next_cursor": null}

{"id": "page_combo_gdd", "space_id": "space_PROD", "parent_id": "page_prod_home", "title": "Combo Fighter \u2014 Game Design Document", "body": "

Combo Fighter is a merge / auto-battler prototype: the player drags Tetris-shaped pieces onto a board, merges matching pieces to upgrade them, connects them into combos, and then watches an auto-battle phase resolve the round. It was the last new concept Harmony Games took to a testable build \u2014 a skeleton crew put a playable MVP together in roughly four to five weeks (late 2025 into January 2026). Of the three prototypes we shipped to store test tracks it posted the strongest early engagement, but it remains parked: we haven't put UA spend behind it yet to see whether that engagement holds at scale.

Core Mechanics

A round has two distinct phases. The build phase is board manipulation; the battle phase is hands-off resolution.

Build phase

  • Drag & place. The tray offers Tetris-shaped pieces (I, L, S, T, square). The player drags a piece onto the board; it snaps to the grid.
  • Merge to upgrade. Two same-tier pieces of the same type that touch merge into the next tier \u2014 the familiar merge-2 loop, but on shaped pieces rather than single cells.
  • Connect for combos. Pieces wired into a contiguous chain form a combo; longer chains grant a battle-phase multiplier, so board layout drives power.

Battle phase

  • The assembled board becomes the player's squad and auto-battles the level's wave. No input during battle \u2014 the round is won or lost on how the board was built.
  • Rewards are gold only. Gold funds re-rolls and starting-piece upgrades. No gems, no energy, no second currency in the MVP.

Ads: None in MVP. There is no ad SDK, no interstitials, and no rewarded placements in the prototype. Monetization was deliberately deferred until the core loop proved it retained \u2014 the test builds measured engagement and retention only.

Art direction

Simple Chibi-style 3D characters on a clean board. The look was chosen to be cheap to produce at prototype scale while still reading as a finished game in a store screenshot.

Scope \u2014 MVP

The build track was a 35-level MVP carved out of a 163-level full design. The MVP existed to answer one question \u2014 does the merge-plus-auto-battle loop hold a player past the first session \u2014 before committing to the remaining content and the deeper progression curve.

  • Shipped in MVP: 35 levels, drag/merge/connect build loop, auto-battle resolution, gold economy, Chibi 3D art.
  • Designed but not built: levels 36\u2013163, meta-progression between runs, monetization surface, live-ops events.

Builds & Early Retention

Three test builds went out over roughly two weeks in January and early February 2026. D1 retention climbed with each build even as install volume swung with test-track promotion.

BuildRelease dateInstallsD1 retention
1.0.62Jan 21, 202612725%
1.0.72Jan 25, 202624431%
1.0.88Feb 4, 20263043%

Session length was the standout signal: Combo Fighter averaged roughly 60 minutes of play on the day of install (D0) \u2014 the best of the three games we prototyped. By 1.0.88 the loop was tightening and D1 had reached 43% on a small install base, but we have not yet validated that at scale on a larger install base.

Related Pages

Prototype targets and the retention bar this work was measured against live in the H1 product objectives: Product OKRs \u2014 2025 H1.

{"id": "page_product_okrs", "space_id": "space_PROD", "parent_id": "page_prod_home", "title": "Product OKRs \u2014 2025 H1", "body": "

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). Scope: H1 2025 product objectives for Zombie Match 3D (store name Puzzles vs Zombies), scored against the metrics bar our investors expect to see before writing a Series A. This is the working scorecard we reviewed at the mid-year checkpoint.

Framing note: these OKRs were deliberately set to the VC bar for a hybrid-casual title \u2014 the numbers a growth investor needs to see (D1 north of 30%, CPI under $5, early ROAS trending toward payback). Hitting internal comfort levels is not the same as clearing a fundable bar. These are the retention and payback bars the team tracks against each half.

Objectives & Key Results

Global launch on May 15, 2025. Everything below is measured on the four weeks after launch unless noted.

Objective / Key ResultTargetActualStatus
Launch ZM3D globallyMay 15, 2025Shipped May 15, 2025✓ Met
D1 retention> 30%28.4% avg (best week ~30.8%)✗ Missed
Blended CPI< $5.00$4.80✓ Met
D30 ROAS> 0.50.31✗ Missed

Acquisition-channel split

The blended D1 of 28.4% hides a real channel gap. Where the users come from matters as much as how many:

  • Facebook \u2014 D1 landing ~34–39%. Higher intent, better early stickiness, but volume is capped at our budget and CPI creeps up as we scale spend.
  • Unity \u2014 D1 landing ~22–26%. Cheaper, far more volume, but the cohorts churn hard by day two. This channel is what drags the blend under the 30% line.

Practically: we can buy the 30% number on Facebook alone, but not at the volume the model needs, and not without pushing CPI past the $4.80 we booked. Unity gives us scale but poisons retention and ROAS.

Retro & conclusion

Candid retro: we cleared the two levers we control tactically (ship date and CPI) and missed the two that decide fundability (retention and ROAS). A 28.4% D1 with a D30 ROAS of 0.31 is a title that does not pay itself back in the window an investor underwrites. The best single week touched 30%, which tells us the ceiling is close — but a one-week peak is not a durable cohort, and we could not hold it once Unity volume was in the blend.

Net: the ZM3D H1 metrics did not clear the bar a growth round is priced on. That result is what drove the decision to pursue a bridge round rather than a priced Series A — buy time to fix Unity-cohort retention and pull D30 ROAS toward 0.5, then re-approach on stronger numbers. Design context and the intended retention loops live in Zombie Match 3D \u2014 Game Design Document.

H2 follow-ups

  • Rework the FTUE for Unity-sourced installs; the day-two cliff is where the blend breaks.
  • Instrument per-channel D7/D30 ROAS separately (in Singular) so we stop hiding a bad cohort inside a passable blend.
  • Re-baseline the D1 > 30% OKR as a per-channel target, not a blended one.

{"id": "page_economy_design", "space_id": "space_PROD", "parent_id": "page_prod_home", "title": "Economy Design \u2014 Coins, Lives & Boosters", "body": "

This page is the cross-game reference for how our soft and hard currencies, lives, and boosters are priced and tuned. It is owned by Design and kept in sync with the individual game design docs \u2014 see Domino Delights \u2014 Game Design Document and Zombie Match 3D \u2014 Game Design Document for the per-game economy layers built on top of these primitives.

Currency model

Every title uses the same two-tier currency so tuning intuition transfers between games. Coins are the soft currency earned in play; gems are the premium hard currency bought or awarded sparingly. The conversion is fixed across the studio:

UnitEqualsNotes
1 US dollar1,000 coinsReference peg for IAP sizing; not a direct store SKU.
1 gem10 coinsHard currency; used for premium sinks and gating.

Level victories pay out roughly 40 gold on average, which anchors the earn side of the loop against the booster sinks below.

Zombie Match 3D item catalog

The ZM3D Master Item List is the source of truth for tunable objects: it currently holds 251 items spread across 23 categories (boosters, tiles, cosmetics, packs, and event-only entitlements). When adding a category, register it here first so the balancing sheet and the client stay aligned.

Booster costs

Boosters are the primary coin sink. Costs are deliberately clustered so players learn the price bands quickly rather than memorizing each item.

BoosterCoin cost
Catapult333
Broom333
Tornado333
Taser333
Glue300
Trampoline200
Super Broom500
  • The four core boosters share the 333 price point so they read as interchangeable power tools.
  • Trampoline is the cheap entry sink at 200 coins to seed early spending habits.
  • Super Broom sits at 500 as the premium clear; it is the main gem-to-coin bridge.

The Domino Delights coin cut (April 2025)

In April 2025 we cut Domino Delights coin rewards by roughly 50% to stop runaway coin inflation. The 99th-percentile daily earn fell from about 25,000 coins to about 9,000 coins. Do not revert reward payouts on GoD without re-running the sink analysis \u2014 the pre-cut curve was unrecoverable.

The symptom was that high-engagement players accumulated coins faster than any sink could absorb, so boosters felt free and the difficulty curve flattened. After the cut, average booster spend nudged up as expected and the coin balance distribution stopped climbing. The changes were applied to the live economy tables under the \"Game of Dominoes\" (GoD) codename and mirrored into this page's tuning constants.

Lives regeneration and refill pricing are game-specific and documented in each GDD. This page only fixes the shared currency and booster primitives.

{"id": "page_analytics_dashboards", "space_id": "space_OPS", "parent_id": "page_ops_home", "title": "Analytics & Metrics Dashboards (Metabase)", "body": "

Owner: Frederick Stone (Growth/UA). This page is the map of our Metabase dashboards. Analysts run everything against the Snowflake BI layer, which is fed from the S3 event lake \u2014 for how telemetry gets from the Unity client into that warehouse, see Analytics Integration \u2014 Unity \u2192 Snowflake.

Metabase is the reporting front-end only \u2014 it holds saved questions and dashboards, not the source of truth. Every card queries Snowflake marts. If a dashboard looks stale, check the warehouse load first (the COPY runs on a schedule), not Metabase.

Standard dashboards

These are the dashboards we keep pinned and review on a regular cadence. They cover the full loop from acquisition through retention and monetization. Names are illustrative \u2014 the actual collection names in Metabase may differ slightly, but the purpose and audience below are what matters.

DashboardPurposeAudience
DAU & RetentionDaily active users, session length, and D1/D7/D30 retention curves by title and cohort.Whole studio; reviewed at Monday standup.
FTUE FunnelFirst-time-user-experience completion \u2014 level start / complete / fail drop-off through the onboarding funnel.Product & game design.
UA / CPI / ROAS by ChannelUser acquisition performance \u2014 spend, installs, blended and per-channel CPI, and D7/D30 ROAS, joined from Singular attribution.Growth/UA (Frederick); exec on investor prep.
Monetization \u2014 IAP / ARPUIn-app-purchase revenue, ARPU / ARPPU, conversion, and Season Pass attach + completion.Product & finance.
Live-Event PerformanceParticipation, completion, and revenue lift per live event vs baseline days.Live-ops & product.

How to read them

  • Every card is date-partitioned; default range is the trailing 28 days. Widen the filter for launch-window cohort views.
  • UA numbers reconcile to Singular, not to store console \u2014 attribution windows differ, so expect small deltas.
  • Retention is measured on activity, not installs; a reinstall inside the window counts as a returning user, not a new one.

Metric definitions live with the OKRs

This page tells you which dashboard to open. It does not define what a metric means. D1 retention, blended CPI, D30 ROAS, ARPU \u2014 those definitions, and the targets we hold them to, are owned alongside the objectives in Product OKRs \u2014 2025 H1. If a dashboard number and an OKR number disagree, the OKR definition wins and the Metabase card is the thing to fix.

Do not fork a dashboard to \"redefine\" a metric for one analysis. If you need a variant (e.g. per-channel D1 instead of blended), add a card to the existing collection so the definition stays traceable. Silent metric drift between a fork and the canonical card is how two people end up quoting different D1 numbers in the same meeting.

Titles currently instrumented into these dashboards: Zombie Match 3D (store name Puzzles vs Zombies), Domino Delights (codename GoD), and Combo Fighter. All three share one event pipeline, so the same dashboard filters to any title.

{"id": "page_analytics_integration", "space_id": "space_ENG", "parent_id": "page_arch_overview", "title": "Analytics Integration — Unity → Snowflake", "body": "

This page documents how gameplay telemetry flows from the Unity client into our analytics warehouse. It is the reference for anyone instrumenting a new event or writing a Snowflake query for a dashboard. For where this sits in the broader system, see Architecture Overview.

Scope: hybrid-casual titles across the studio — Domino Delights (codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes"), Zombie Match 3D ("Puzzles vs Zombies" on store), and Combo Fighter. All three share one instrumentation library and one pipeline.

Pipeline overview

The Unity client emits events through the Firebase Analytics SDK. From there a game-analytics pipeline streams events into AWS, transforms them, and lands them in object storage, from which the warehouse loads. The stages:

  • Unity client → Firebase — the client batches events and hands them to the Firebase Analytics SDK on-device.
  • Firebase → Kinesis — events are forwarded into an AWS Kinesis stream for ingestion.
  • Kinesis → Glue — an AWS Glue job validates and transforms records (flattens the event envelope, casts types, partitions by date).
  • Glue → S3 — both a raw/ and a processed/ prefix are written to S3.
  • S3 → Snowflake — the BI/warehouse layer loads from the S3 processed/ prefix. Analysts query Snowflake for dashboards and ad-hoc analysis.

Install attribution is handled separately by Singular (our MMP); attribution results are joined into Snowflake for UA reporting rather than flowing through the client event stream.

Event categories

Every event carries a common envelope (app version, platform, device class, session id, server timestamp). At a high level events fall into five categories:

CategoryFires onUsed for
SessionApp open / close, foreground / backgroundDAU, session length, retention curves
ProgressionLevel start / complete / failDifficulty tuning, funnel drop-off
Resource / economyCurrency and life grant / spendSink-source balance, economy health
Ad impressionRewarded / interstitial shown & completedAd revenue, fill rate, eCPM
Client errorHandled exceptions, load stallsCrash triage, release health

Load macro (Glue → S3 → Snowflake)

The warehouse pulls the Glue output from S3 with a scheduled COPY. Sketch of the load:

sql

The COPY is append-only and idempotent per partition — never TRUNCATE the landing table to "reload", or you drop history the marts depend on. Backfills replay a specific dt= partition only.

Adding or changing an event

  • Register the event name and payload in the shared instrumentation library before shipping — do not free-type event names in game code.
  • New fields must be nullable; the Glue transform tolerates extra keys but will not backfill missing ones.
  • Flag any type change (int → string, etc.) to eng before release — it breaks the Snowflake COPY column mapping.

{"id": "page_qa_runbook", "space_id": "space_ENG", "parent_id": "page_eng_home", "title": "QA Regression Runbook", "body": "

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Owned by QA (Vincent); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, "Game of Dominoes"), Zombie Match 3D (store name "Puzzles vs Zombies") and Combo Fighter. Keep it to ~45 minutes per title; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 ZM3D progression wipe only reproduced when updating from a previously-shipped version — a clean install looked perfectly healthy. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 ZM3D froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets. Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory — N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 ZM3D)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe reproduced on update only
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account; confirm entitlements restore

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release — fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

Per-title regression matrix

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

AreaCheckExpectedDominoZM3DCombo
First-time UXFresh install → tutorial → first winNo stall; tutorial completes; first level winnableYesYesYes
Font / localisationCold start on a fresh device (no cached font)UI renders; no blank/boxed glyphs at ~22% loadYesYesn/a
ProgressionPlay 3 levels, force-quit, relaunchLevel and currency persist; no reset to level 1YesYesYes
EconomyEarn + spend coins, buy a boosterBalances reconcile; booster consumed onceYesYesn/a
Live-opsEnter the active event; complete a questEvent loads; quest ticks; rewards grantedYesYesn/a
IAPSandbox purchase + restoreReceipt validated; entitlement restored on reinstallYesYesn/a
AdsWatch a rewarded ad to completionReward granted once; no double-grant on retryYesYesn/a

Known-issue regression cases

These are the incidents that have bitten us in production; every one now has a permanent regression case so it cannot silently return. Reproduce the trigger, confirm the fix holds.

Font-download stall. On a fresh device the dynamic font pack could fail to download, freezing the UI at ~22% of the tutorial. Regression: install on a wiped device with a throttled connection; confirm a fallback font renders and load continues.

Progression reset. A device-identifier change once wiped returning players back to level 1. Regression: migrate a save across a reinstall; confirm the cloud save rehydrates and no reset occurs.

Quest not resetting / not populating. A bad deploy left the daily quest board empty. Regression: roll the clock across a UTC day boundary; confirm quests repopulate and completion state resets.

Device lab

The minimum matrix is one recent + one old device per platform. We keep a small physical lab plus a cloud device farm for the long tail.

PlatformRecentOld / min-specTablet
iOScurrent-gen iPhone, latest OSiPhone SE-class, oldest supported OSiPad (one gen)
Androidcurrent-gen Samsung / Pixellow-RAM device, oldest supported OSone Android tablet

Sign-off

QA posts the completed matrix in #ops and links it from the release ticket. A build without a green matrix does not get submitted — no exceptions during the weekday release window, and never on a Friday.

{"id": "page_release_checklist", "space_id": "space_OPS", "parent_id": "page_ops_home", "title": "Release Checklist & Store Submission", "body": "

Owner: Vincent Parker (QA) · Space: OPS. This is the gate every Harmony Games title passes before we submit a build to the App Store or Google Play. It applies to Zombie Match 3D (store name \"Puzzles vs Zombies\"), Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \"Game of Dominoes\") and Combo Fighter. Do not submit a build until every box below is ticked and QA has signed off — the checklist exists because every item on it maps to a real incident that shipped.

Always test the UPDATE path from the last two shipped versions (N-1 and N-2), not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression wipe reproduced only when updating over a previously-shipped build; a clean install looked perfectly healthy. A fresh-install-only pass does not clear this gate.

Pre-submission checklist

Build & QA

  • Full manual regression is green on real iOS and Android hardware — see the QA Regression Runbook. QA sign-off is a hard gate.
  • Update path verified from N-1 and N-2: level, coins and unlocks survive the update; no save/progression loss.
  • Splash and loading screen watched all the way to gameplay on a throttled connection and with the app cache cleared — no stall (see incidents below).
  • Live quest config, if touched, has passed QA and a canary — nothing pushed straight to the live quest server (see the Quest System \u2014 Design & Incident Postmortem).

Store metadata & compliance

  • Version and build number bumped; release notes drafted for both stores.
  • Screenshots, age rating and data-safety / privacy declarations current.
  • IAP products and prices active in App Store Connect and Play Console before submission.
  • Analytics build tagged so installs attribute correctly (Singular).

Domino Delights is in maintenance mode — the current build is tracked under ENG-2366 (Jul 2025): IAP catalog refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, and the lives regeneration fix. Run the same update-path and store checks against it; maintenance does not mean unreviewed.

Lessons from incidents

Each row is a bug that reached players. Treat the corresponding checklist item as non-negotiable.

TicketTitle / dateWhat happenedChecklist item it hardened
ENG-2346ZM3D global launch, May 15 2025Remote font/asset download made the game look frozen at ~22% on the splash screen. Fixed by changing when fonts load and adding a downloading indicator.Watch splash to gameplay on a slow connection with cache cleared.
ENG-2343ZM3D global launch, May 15 2025Splash / loading screen resolution issue at launch.Verify splash and loading render correctly across device resolutions.
—Progression wipe, June 2025Player progression wiped on update; reproduced on the update path only, not fresh install.Test update from N-1 and N-2; confirm save/progression integrity.
ENG-2366Domino Delights maintenance, Jul 2025Maintenance build: IAP refresh, difficulty tuning, interstitials disabled, lives fix.Run full store + update checks even on maintenance-mode builds.

When any check fails, block the release, file the bug with device / OS / source build, and do not ship until it is green.

parameters.title: Combo Fighter UA Scale-Readiness Decision Pack
parameters.bodyText:
Combo Fighter UA Scale-Readiness Decision Pack

OVERALL DECISION: HOLD (DO NOT OPEN SPEND)

1. BLOCKER GAPS (SUMMARY & EVIDENCE)
--------------------------------------------------
Gap 1: Unvalidated D1 Retention at Scale
- Evidence: Build 1.0.62 achieved 25% D1 retention (missing the >30% OKR bar). Build 1.0.72 reached 31% D1 retention on a thin sample size of 244 installs. The GDD explicitly notes that retention has not been validated on a scale-sized install base.

Gap 2: D0 Play Time (Session Length) Discrepancy
- Evidence: GDD claims ~60 minutes D0 play time ("averaged roughly 60 minutes of play on the day of install"), but actual workbook records in "Combo Fighter Design Details.xlsx" (Versions tab) show 48.74 minutes for Build 1.0.62 and 42.98 minutes for Build 1.0.72.

Combo Fighter UA Scale-Readiness Decision Pack

OVERALL DECISION: HOLD (DO NOT OPEN SPEND)

1. BLOCKER GAPS (SUMMARY & EVIDENCE)
--------------------------------------------------
Gap 1: Unvalidated D1 Retention at Scale

# Combo Fighter UA Scale-Readiness Decision Pack

**OVERALL DECISION: HOLD (DO NOT OPEN SPEND)**

---

## 1. BLOCKER GAPS (ITEM BY ITEM)

### **Gap 1: Unvalidated D1

Retention at Scale**
* **Status:** HOLD
* **Evidence / Source:** In-window Build `1.0.62
` achieved only **25% D1 retention** (missing the Product OKRs bar of `> 30%`). In
-window Build `1.0.72` reached **31% D1 retention**, but on a thin sample size of only
**244 installs**. As explicitly stated in the Game Design Document (*Combo Fighter — Game Design Document*): *"
By 1.0.88 the loop was tightening and D1 had reached 43% on a small install

base, but we have not yet validated that at scale on a larger install base."*
* **Linear Issue:**

`ENG-2440`

---

### **Gap 2: D0 Play Time (Session Length
Combo Fighter — Game Design Document*) claims: *"Session length was the standout signal: Combo Fighter averaged roughly 60 minutes
of play on the day of install (D0) — the best of the three games we prototyped."* However
, actual telemetry recorded in the Drive workbook (*Combo Fighter Design Details.xlsx* → `Versions` tab) shows Build
`1.0.62` averaged **48.74 minutes** and Build `1.0.
72` averaged **42.98 minutes**. Neither in-window build reached the 60-minute claim.

* **Linear Issue:** `ENG-2439`

---

### **Gap 3: In

-Window Codebase Ad SDK & Monetization Conflicts**
* **Status:** HOLD
* **Evidence / Source:**
The Game Design Document (*Combo Fighter — Game Design Document*) mandates an unmonetized MVP gate: *"Ads:
None in MVP. There is no ad SDK, no interstitials, and no rewarded placements in the prototype. Monetization was
deliberately deferred until the core loop proved it retained — the test builds measured engagement and retention only."* However, an inspection
of the GitHub repository (`harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters`) revealed **four merged in-window pull requests** that introduced ad

SDKs and rewarded ad flows directly into the codebase prior to the January 27, 2026 cutoff:
  * **PR
#24** (Merged Jan 13, 2026): *"AppLovinMAX integration and Rewarded

Ads"* — Integrated AppLovinMAX SDK and rewarded placements.
  * **PR #26** (Merged Jan 15
, 2026): *"Added cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch"* — Implemented ad watch cooldown timers

for upgrade discounts.
  * **PR #28** (Merged Jan 17, 202

6): *"Main Menu Updates"* — Added ad timer icons, upgrade ad buttons, and ad pricing displays.
  * **PR #3
0** (Merged Jan 17, 2026): *"fixing upgrade button alpha when disabled"* —

UI adjustments for upgrade ad discount buttons.
* **Linear Issue:** `ENG-2442`

* **Status:** HOLD
* **
Evidence / Source:** An exhaustive sweep across all Linear teams (`ART`, `DES`, `ENG`, `EPI`, `ZOM

* **Linear Issue:** `ENG-2441`

**Gap 5: Absence of Dedicated Combo Paid-UA Card on Trello UA/BD Board**

* **Linear Issue:** `ENG-2443
